config.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard

intro.title: Design Real-Time Dashboard
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a real-time dashboard that displays live-updating data, such as user activity or metrics. You will learn how to use React state and the useEffect hook to fetch and update data at regular intervals. The main technologies involved are React components, state management, and asynchronous JavaScript with setInterval. By the end, you'll have a functional dashboard that automatically refreshes its content to simulate real-time data.
intro.usecase: Real-time dashboards are essential in modern applications where live data visualization drives decision-making. Developers implement these patterns in analytics platforms like Google Analytics dashboards, financial trading interfaces showing stock fluctuations, and operations monitoring tools like AWS CloudWatch. These dashboards typically feature auto-updating charts, live metrics, and interactive filters that respond instantly to data changes. Mastering this pattern prepares you to build the responsive, data-driven interfaces that users expect in today's web applications.

objectives: Initialize and manage state variables for real-time dashboard metrics using React hooks
Construct responsive UI components to display live data visualizations
Implement event handlers to update dashboard metrics based on user interactions
Configure data binding between state variables and dashboard display elements
Integrate mock data streams to simulate real-time data updates
Manipulate component rendering based on changing data conditions
Apply conditional styling to highlight critical metric thresholds

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building your real-time dashboard component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Dashboard that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called Dashboard that returns JSX containing a div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Dashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Dashboard component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The Dashboard component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Dashboard and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component isn't defined correctly. Check the function name and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize dashboard data state
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'dashboardData' with initial values for users, revenue, and sessions.
steps.hint: Initialize the state with an object containing numeric values for these three metrics.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an object
const [userData, setUserData] = useState({ name: 'John', age: 25 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboardData state variable should be initialized with an object containing users, revenue, and sessions properties.
successCriteria: dashboardData state is declared using useState with initial values for users, revenue, and sessions
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure dashboardData is initialized as an object with all three properties: users, revenue, and sessions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dashboardData state isn't properly initialized. Use useState to create a state variable with initial values for users, revenue, and sessions.

steps.title: Define update function for metrics
steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, define a function called updateMetrics that updates the dashboardData state with new random values.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setDashboardData to update the state. You can generate random values for metrics like users, revenue, and sessions.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named updateMetrics is defined inside the Dashboard component that updates dashboardData state with new values.
successCriteria: The updateMetrics function is defined and uses setDashboardData to update the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your updateMetrics function uses setDashboardData to update the state with new values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetrics function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that updates the dashboardData state using setDashboardData.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your Dashboard component's return statement, replace the current `null` with a `<div>` element that has a class name of 'dashboard-container' and contains an `<h1>` header with the text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
steps.hint: The return statement should now output a div with a className attribute and an h1 element inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component now returns a structured container with a header, establishing the basic layout for the dashboard.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div with className='dashboard-container' and an h1 with the text 'Real-Time Dashboard'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the div with the correct className and the h1 header with the exact text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't match the required structure. Check that you replaced null with a div containing an h1.

steps.title: Add metrics display section
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your Dashboard component, add a <div> element that displays the current users, revenue, and sessions values from the dashboardData state.
steps.hint: You can access the values using dashboardData.users, dashboardData.revenue, and dashboardData.sessions. Place them inside JSX curly braces {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The return statement now contains a div that displays the three dashboard metrics from state.
successCriteria: A div element is added inside the return statement that shows dashboardData.users, dashboardData.revenue, and dashboardData.sessions values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying all three values (users, revenue, sessions) from the dashboardData state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics display section isn't quite right. Check that you're returning a div element that shows the three values from dashboardData state.

steps.title: Style metrics with CSS classes
steps.instruction: Add CSS class names to the metrics elements in your return statement for proper styling.
steps.hint: Use the className attribute to assign CSS classes to your HTML elements. For example: <div className="metric-card">
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding CSS classes to elements

Dashboard

Real-time metrics
steps.expectedOutcome: The metrics display section will have CSS class names applied to the container and metric elements for styling.
successCriteria: All three metric containers have className attributes with appropriate class names (e.g., 'metric-card').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some CSS classes, but not all metric containers have className attributes. Make sure all three metric divs have appropriate class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: No CSS classes were added to the metric elements. Remember to use the className attribute on your div elements to assign styling classes.

steps.title: Add update button
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Update Metrics' inside the main container, after the metrics display section.
steps.hint: Place the button after the three metric divs, but still inside the outer div that wraps everything.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Update Metrics' appears below the three metrics in the dashboard.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Update Metrics' is added to the component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Update Metrics'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with text 'Update Metrics' is missing from the dashboard.

steps.title: Add real-time indicator
steps.instruction: Add a status indicator element that shows 'Live' when metrics are recent. Place it above the metrics display section.
steps.hint: You can add a <div> with a class name like 'status-indicator' and text content 'Live'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a status indicator element
Live
steps.expectedOutcome: A status indicator element with the text 'Live' appears above the metrics display.
successCriteria: The status indicator element is added with appropriate content and placement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's a status indicator with the text 'Live' placed above the metrics.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status indicator element is missing or incorrectly placed. Try adding a <div> with 'Live' text above the metrics section.

steps.title: Export Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Export the Dashboard component as the default export from this file.
steps.hint: Add an export statement at the end of your file to make the Dashboard component available for use in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component is exported and ready to be imported and used in other parts of your application.
successCriteria: Dashboard component is exported as the default export from the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax for the Dashboard component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component needs to be exported. Add an export statement at the end of your file.
